survey_claim: Key evaluativist source: unpleasantness represents bodily damage as bad
finding: Yes, with refinements: badness is subject-relative and graded ('apt to harm'); paper never uses 'evaluativism' (B1 §2)

survey_claim: Unpleasantness is a command: 'protect this body part / stop this'
finding: Command targets bodily damage, not the pain; 'protect this body part' is Klein's wording (B2 §1)

survey_claim: Imperativism explains motivational force and uninformativeness; content action-directed
finding: Matches chapter 1, but the theory concerns pain per se, not unpleasantness; 12 of ~200 pages held (B2 §2)

survey_claim: Key evaluativist source: unpleasantness as evaluation of damage as bad
finding: Matches; evaluation is experiential and itself motivating; represented condition left open (B2 §4)

survey_claim: Evaluativism predicts a valenced judgement that causes motivation but is not itself motivational
finding: Review never discusses evaluativism; Bain's own 2017 chapter says the experience is itself motivational (B2 §5)

survey_claim: Klein: the command is issued but no longer binding
finding: Matches p. 510; offered as best candidate, not a full defence (C §1)

survey_claim: Counter-reading: asymbolia isn't pain at all
finding: Title says so; body argues only that evidence fails to show it is pain, provisionally (C §2)

survey_claim: Affective and motivational used interchangeably; the fusion was inherited
finding: 'Motivational' never appears; the explicit fusion is in talbot2019, which misattributes it to Price (D §2, D §4)

survey_claim: Components not independently modifiable; ratings covary; dissociations mostly attention effects
finding: Asymmetric verdict (affect might be modifiable); explanations offered are demand, wording, bias, not attention (D §4)

survey_claim: Suggestion moves unpleasantness with intensity fixed; ACC not S1 changes
finding: Matches, with 'fixed' meaning not significantly different (E1 §1)

survey_claim: The reverse suggestion moves S1
finding: S1 moved, but unpleasantness moved too (r=0.81) and authors reject a simple dichotomy (E1 §2)

survey_claim: Mu-opioid signalling regulates the two dimensions in different regions
finding: Between-person correlations with overlapping regions and no direct test (E1 §3)

survey_claim: Attending to location vs unpleasantness dissociates lateral vs medial systems
finding: Matches; rests on attention manipulation, S1 effect at P=0.05 corrected (E1 §4)

survey_claim: Dopamine-precursor depletion changes affect but not sensation
finding: Matches; affect effect is one post-task rating at p=.048 (E1 §5)

survey_claim: Opioids: unpleasantness down, intensity flat (cited as pain evidence)
finding: Direction right but the sensation was experimentally induced breathlessness, not pain (E2 §1)

survey_claim: In mice, S1->ACC projections carry sensory into affective circuitry
finding: Content matches the authors' conclusion; animals were rats (E2 §2)

survey_claim: Unnamed '7T/EEG' result: cortex relates more to unpleasantness than intensity
finding: Direction matches; 7T fMRI only, no EEG; authors call the difference gradual (E2 §3)

survey_claim: Emotional priming moves unpleasantness not intensity, with distinct ERP components
finding: Matches; intensity quadratic trend p=.04; both N2 and P2 changed, only P2 predicted (E2 §4)

survey_claim: The fear-avoidance model across four iterations
finding: Paper reviews two earlier models and credits Lethem 1983; counts no iterations (F §1)

survey_claim: The fear-avoidance model across four iterations
finding: Evidence review with a merged diagram; counts no iterations (F §3)

survey_claim: The fear-avoidance model across four iterations
finding: Calls for a next generation in words; no new diagram; counts no iterations (F §4)

survey_claim: The fear-avoidance model across four iterations
finding: Pictorial restatement anchored to Vlaeyen & Linton 2012; counts no iterations (F §6)

survey_claim: Recasts pain as a homeostatic emotion
finding: Matches p. 303 (F §2)

survey_claim: Experimental work measures avoidance as behaviour: pain-avoidance vs reward-seeking
finding: Matches; headline is that behaviour and self-reported fear came apart (F §5)

survey_claim: ACC lesions abolish pain place avoidance without changing nociceptive thresholds
finding: Rostral ACC only; no thresholds measured, acute formalin behaviour instead (G1 §1)

survey_claim: ACC activation is itself an aversive teaching signal
finding: Matches; authors call evidence not conclusive; one dose, one paradigm (G1 §2)

survey_claim: BLA ensemble encodes unpleasantness; silencing removes affective behaviour not reflexes
finding: Matches, but acute effect is a reduction, not removal (G1 §3)

survey_claim: ACC->PAG projections required for pain avoidance: a command line, not evaluative
finding: Necessity never tested; command-vs-evaluative contrast is not the paper's; paper says ACC encodes unpleasantness (G1 §4)

survey_claim: Wiech & Tracey's motivational perspective
finding: It is that review (G2 §1)

survey_claim: Model-based and model-free routes of pain-avoidance learning
finding: Matches; omits that pain-vs-reward difference is provisional and no neural data (G2 §2)

survey_claim: Review on emotional-motivational processing
finding: It is that review (G2 §3)

survey_claim: Core function motivational; pain a precision-weighted RL control signal
finding: First half verbatim; 'precision' means precise and objectifiable, 'precision-weighted' never appears (G2 §4)

survey_claim: Human pain-avoidance behaviour has neural correlates distinct from pain report
finding: Study never compares avoidance with pain report; claim is parietal rather than PAG role (G2 §5)

survey_claim: Pain-avoidance learning has its own neural systems for received vs avoided pain
finding: Matches; authors' wording is 'suggest', drug effects only in model parameters (G2 §6)

survey_claim: Individual differences in avoidance vs reward learning
finding: Models both in one task, not a single avoidance-vs-reward dimension; title truncated (G2 §7)

survey_claim: Distinct voxel populations and networks for valence and intensity; no action axis
finding: Accurate; populations lie within the same regions and 'intensity' is affective (H §1)

survey_claim: Cleanest demonstration that avoidance is separate from both ratings (N=62)
finding: 58 analysed; authors say the pattern does not allow a differential conclusion; task-compliance confound (H §2)

survey_claim: Adaptive control hypothesis: aMCC integrates pain, affect and control
finding: Matches; framed as working hypothesis on indirect inferences (I §1)

survey_claim: Mid-cingulate region whose pain activity scales with action processing
finding: Shows action dependence, not graded scaling; RT link not pain-specific (I §2)

survey_claim: Motor control and pain in MCC
finding: Matches p. 1906 (I §3)

survey_claim: Facial pain expressions drive motor mirroring in MCC
finding: Reverses the conclusion: pain responses appear with attention to meaning; affective-meaning networks favoured (I §4)

survey_claim: The midcingulate motor map
finding: A motor map exists but evidence is juice-reward feedback; pain only a hypothesis (I §5)

survey_claim: Causal cingulotomy evidence (used for pain and action)
finding: Lesions predicted facial-emotion and Stroop errors in depression; pain never measured (I §6)

survey_claim: Empathy for pain motivates action with motor-dynamic signatures
finding: Matches; change is in vigour of an instructed press (I §7)

survey_claim: Extended in C-afferent mutation carriers
finding: Matches; 12 per group, fixed-effects model (I §8)

survey_claim: Prediction and action in cortical pain processing
finding: Matches title; preregistered action tests null, action dependence exploratory (I §9)

survey_claim: SCAN named without a source
finding: This is the defining paper; pain link is by citation only (I §10)
